ml-linreg-origin-06: No intercept wala model hai — line origin se guzregi, toh centred-sum wala slope nahi lagega.
$\sum x^2 = 1+4+9 = 14$. Ab $\sum xy$ term-by-term jodo. Trap: $\sum y/\sum x$ ek alag (galat) ratio hai.
ml-linreg-origin-07: Model origin se guzarta hai — chaar sums diye hain par sabke sab kaam ke nahi.
No-intercept fit: $w = \sum xy/\sum x^2$, phir $\hat y = 3w$. $\sum x$ aur $\sum y$ sirf intercept wale model mein lagte.
$\sum xy = 50$, $\sum x^2 = 20$ — ratio sahi direction mein lo. Trap: $\sum y/\sum x$ wala slope mat lena.
ml-linreg-origin-08: Model $x$ mein linear nahi, par $w$ mein linear hai — naya feature $\phi = 1/x$ socho.
$\hat y = w\phi$ ke liye $w = \sum\phi y/\sum\phi^2$, jahan $\phi = 1, 0.5, 0.25$.
$\sum\phi y = 4(1) + 2.5(0.5) + 1(0.25) = 5.5$. Ab $\sum\phi^2$ nikaalo. Trap: denominator mein $\sum\phi$ nahi, $\sum\phi^2$ aata hai.
ml-linreg-origin-09: Har option alag se check karo: pehle $w$ nikaalo, phir residuals, phir naye point ka asar.
$w = \sum xy/\sum x^2$ with $x = 1,2,3$, $y = 2,2,6$. No intercept ho toh guarantee sirf $\sum x_ie_i = 0$ ki hai.
$\sum x^2 = 14$, $\sum xy = 2+4+18$. Point $(0, 5)$ ke liye socho: $x = 0$ wala point dono sums mein kitna jodta hai? Trap: residual $= y - \hat y$, ulta mat lo.
ml-linreg-origin-10: Yahan ulta sawaal hai: $w$ diya hai, ek data value $k$ dhoondhni hai — formula ko equation ki tarah use karo.
$w = \sum xy/\sum x^2$ with $\sum xy = 1\cdot1 + 2\cdot4 + 3k$ and $\sum x^2 = 1+4+9$.
$\sum xy = 9 + 3k$, $\sum x^2 = 14$; ab $(9+3k)/14 = 2$ solve karo. Trap: teesra point line $y = 2x$ pe hi ho, ye zaroori nahi.
ml-linreg-origin-11: Ek term $(y_i - wx_i)^2$ ko $w$ ke respect mein differentiate karna hai — chain rule ka inner part dhyaan se.
$\frac{du}{dw}$ nikaalo: $y_i$ constant hai, $-wx_i$ ka derivative kya? Trap: inner factor ka sign aur $x_i$ dono rakhne hain.
ml-linreg-origin-12: Dono models ka relation dekho: kya ek model doosre ka special case hai?
Origin line = intercept model with $a = 0$. Bade set pe liya gaya minimum chhote set ke minimum se zyada nahi ho sakta.
Socho: $\text{SSE}_1$ ka minimum kin $(a, b)$ pe liya gaya — kya $(0, w)$ bhi usme shaamil hai? Trap: equality sirf special data pe hoti hai.
ml-linreg-ols-07: Intercept ke saath fit hai — slope ke liye centred sums ($x - \bar x$, $y - \bar y$) chahiye.
$b = S_{xy}/S_{xx}$ with $S_{xy} = \sum(x - \bar x)(y - \bar y)$; yahan $\bar x = 5$, $\bar y = 7.5$.
Deviations: $x - \bar x = -3, -1, 1, 3$ aur $y - \bar y = -4.5, -0.5, 0.5, 4.5$. Ab products jodo. Trap: $\sum xy/\sum x^2$ sirf origin wale model ka formula hai.
ml-linreg-ols-08: Sirf means aur slope diye hain — intercept khud nikaalna padega, ek khaas point use karke.
OLS line $(\bar x, \bar y)$ se guzarti hai: $a = \bar y - b\bar x$, toh $\hat y = \bar y + b(x - \bar x)$.
$a = 50 - 3 \times 10$ nikaalo, phir $x = 12$ daalo. Trap: $a$ mein plus sign lagana ya $a$ bhool jaana — dono common galti.
ml-linreg-ols-09: Total variation $S_{yy}$ do hisson mein bant-ta hai: jo line explain karti hai aur jo residual bachta hai.
Intercept ke saath $\text{SSE} = S_{yy} - S_{xy}^2/S_{xx}$; yahan $S_{xy} = 20$, $S_{xx} = 10$, $S_{yy} = 50$.
Explained part $= S_{xy}^2/S_{xx} = 400/10$. Ab ise total se ghatao. Trap: explained part ko hi SSE mat likhna, aur $1 - R^2$ ek fraction hai, sum nahi.
ml-linreg-ols-10: Sirf $y$ badla hai, linear tarike se — har quantity ($b$, $a$, residuals, $R^2$) pe asar alag se dekho.
Centring mein $+3$ cancel hota hai: $y' - \bar y' = 2(y - \bar y)$. Formulas: $b = S_{xy}/S_{xx}$, $a = \bar y - b\bar x$, $R^2 = 1 - \text{SSE}/S_{yy}$.
Residual dekho: $e' = 2y + 3 - (a' + b'x)$ ko $e$ ke terms mein likho. Trap: residual double ho toh squared residual kitna guna hoga?
ml-linreg-ols-11: Ek hi data pe do regressions — dono slopes ka numerator same hai: $S_{xy}$.
Dono slopes multiply karke dekho ki $S_{xx}$, $S_{yy}$ kahan baith-te hain, phir numbers daalo. Trap: $r$ aur $R^2$ alag hain — square-root mat lena.
ml-linreg-ols-12: Prediction chahiye, toh pehle poori line ($a$ aur $b$) nikaalo — intercept wala model hai.
$b = S_{xy}/S_{xx}$, $a = \bar y - b\bar x$; yahan $\bar x = 3$, $\bar y = 4$.
Deviations: $x - \bar x = -2,-1,0,1,2$ aur $y - \bar y = -2, 0, 1, 0, 1$; products jodke $S_{xy}$ banao. Trap: intercept pe ruk mat jaana, $x = 6$ daalna hai.
ml-ridge-06: Ridge fit pehle, prediction baad mein — penalty $\lambda w^2$ ki wajah se OLS slope nahi chalega.
1-D ridge: $w = \sum xy/(\sum x^2 + \lambda)$ with $\lambda = 6$; phir $\hat y = 4w$.
$\sum x^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14$; ab $\sum xy$ nikaalo aur denominator $14 + 6$ lo. Trap: $w$ pe ruk mat jaana — $x = 4$ pe prediction chahiye.
ml-ridge-07: Dhyaan do: penalty sirf slope $w$ pe hai, intercept $b$ pe nahi.
$\lambda \to \infty$ pe $w \to 0$; bacha hua loss $\sum (y_i - b)^2$ sirf $b$ ka function hai.
$\frac{d}{db}\sum (y_i - b)^2 = 0$ set karo aur dekho $b$ kya banta hai. Trap: intercept penalised nahi hai, toh prediction 0 nahi jaata.
ml-ridge-08: $X^\top X$ diagonal nahi hai (off-diagonal 1) — har weight alag se divide karke nahi milega, 2×2 inverse chahiye.
$w = (X^\top X + \lambda I)^{-1}X^\top y$; $\lambda I$ sirf diagonal mein judta hai: matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$.
2×2 inverse: $\frac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$, yahan det $= 8$. Ise $(4, 2)$ se multiply karo, pehli row lo. Trap: $\lambda$ off-diagonal mein mat jodo.
ml-ridge-09: Dono formulas likh ke compare karo — numerator same hai, denominator ka farak dekho.
$w_0 = \sum xy/\sum x^2$ aur $w_\lambda = \sum xy/(\sum x^2 + \lambda)$; training SSE ka minimiser sirf $w_0$ hai.
Example lo: $\sum x^2 = 10$, $\lambda = 5$ vs $10$ — denominator 15 se 20 hua, kya double hua? Trap: ridge weight 0 ki taraf jaata hai, sign nahi badalta.
ml-ridge-10: Objective ki minimum value poochi hai, sirf $w$ nahi — dono parts (squared error + penalty) jodne honge.
Pehle $w = \sum xy/(\sum x^2 + \lambda)$ with $\sum xy = 8$, $\sum x^2 = 5$, $\lambda = 3$; phir $J(w)$ evaluate karo.
$w$ nikaalke residuals $2 - w$ aur $3 - 2w$ banao, square karke jodo. Trap: penalty $\lambda w^2$ jodna mat bhoolo, aur OLS wala $w$ mat daalo.
ml-ridge-11: Sirf penalty term $\lambda\lVert w\rVert^2$ ka gradient chahiye, aur update mein uska sign.
$\frac{\partial}{\partial w_j}\lambda\sum_k w_k^2 = 2\lambda w_j$; update hai $w \leftarrow w - \eta\,\nabla J$.
$2\lambda w$ ko $-\eta$ se multiply karo aur $w$ ke saath combine karke dekho. Trap: $\text{sign}(w)$ wala step L1 ka hai, L2 ka nahi.
ml-ridge-12: Do rows hain — training aur validation. $\lambda$ choose karne ke liye kaunsi row dekhni chahiye?
Rule: hyperparameter wahi jo validation error minimum kare; ridge mein training error to $\lambda$ ke saath badhta hi hai.
$\lambda = 0.01$ dekho: training 2.0 par validation 8.0 — ye gap kya batata hai? Ab baaki $\lambda$ ki validation values compare karo. Trap: sabse kam training MSE wala $\lambda$ overfit karta hai.
ml-logistic-07: Class 0 ki probability poochi hai, class 1 ki nahi — aakhri step mein dhyaan rakho.
$z = 1\cdot2 - 2\cdot1 + 0.5\cdot4 - 1$ nikaalo, phir sigmoid lagao. Trap: bias mat bhoolo, aur $\sigma(z)$ pe ruk mat jaana.
ml-logistic-08: Logistic model mein $x$ ka seedha linear asar kis cheez pe hota hai — $p$ pe, odds pe ya log-odds pe?
$\ln\frac{p}{1-p} = w^\top x + b$; $x_3 \to x_3 + 1$ karne se right side mein $w_3$ judta hai.
Log-odds mein $+0.7$ hua; ab dono side ka exponent lo aur dekho odds pe kya hota hai. Trap: probability pe ye seedha multiply ya add nahi hota.
ml-logistic-09: Do probabilities di hain — inhe log-odds mein badlo, kyunki wahi $x$ mein linear hai.
Do equations: $w + b = 0$ aur $3w + b = \ln 4$; inhe solve karke $x = 5$ pe $z$ nikaalo. Trap: probability ko seedhi line pe extrapolate mat karo.
ml-logistic-10: $z$ ka sign badla hai — sigmoid ki symmetry kaam aayegi, poora calculation dobara nahi chahiye.
Identity: $\sigma(-z) = 1 - \sigma(z)$ (graph point $(0, 0.5)$ ke around symmetric hai).
$\sigma(-2) = 1/(1 + e^{2})$ likho aur $\sigma(2) = 1/(1 + e^{-2})$ se compare karo. Trap: sigmoid ka output kabhi negative ya 1 se bada nahi hota.
ml-logistic-11: Har option ke liye $z = 2x_1 - x_2 + 1$ nikaalo; threshold 0.5 ka matlab boundary $z = 0$.
Rule: $p > 0.5 \iff z > 0$, aur $\sigma$ increasing hai, toh coefficient ka sign hi direction batata hai.
$(0, 1)$ pe $z$ daalo; $(1, 0)$ pe $z$ nikaal ke $\sigma(z)$ ko 0.9 se compare karo. Trap: saare coefficients scale karne se kya line $z = 0$ badalti hai?
ml-logistic-12: Ek SGD step hai: pehle current $\hat p$, phir gradient, phir update — teen kaam.
Cross-entropy ke liye $\nabla_w L = (\hat p - y)\,x$; update $w \leftarrow w - \eta\,\nabla_w L$ with $\eta = 0.5$.
$z = 0.5\cdot2 - 1\cdot1 = 0$, toh $\hat p = \sigma(0) = 0.5$. Ab $(\hat p - y)x_1$ banao aur update karo. Trap: minus sign aur $\eta$ dono lagane hain.
ml-logistic-13: Har pair ke liye socho: model ne **true class** ko kitni probability di?
$y = 1$ pe loss $-\ln\hat p$, $y = 0$ pe loss $-\ln(1 - \hat p)$; $-\ln$ decreasing hai, toh chhoti probability = bada loss.
Pehla pair: $y = 0$, $\hat p = 0.7$, toh true class ko $0.3$ mila. Baaki teen ka bhi aise hi nikaalo. Trap: $y = 0$ ke liye $\hat p$ nahi, $1 - \hat p$ dekhna hai.
ml-logistic-14: Threshold 0.5 nahi, 0.9 hai — toh $z > 0$ wala rule nahi chalega.
$\ln 9 = 2\ln 3$ aur $\ln 3 \approx 1.10$ se cut-off nikaalo, phir har $z$ compare karo. Trap: $z$ ko seedha 0.9 se compare mat karo.
ml-logistic-15: Char alag properties — har ek ko formula $\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ se seedha test karo.
Kaam ke facts: $\sigma' = \sigma(1 - \sigma)$, aur $\ln\frac{\sigma(z)}{1 - \sigma(z)} = z$ (logit, sigmoid ka inverse).
$z = 0$ daal ke $\sigma(0)$ aur $\sigma'(0)$ nikaalo. Increasing ke liye socho: kya $\sigma(1 - \sigma)$ kabhi negative ho sakta hai? Trap: range $(0, 1)$ sigmoid ki hai, log-odds ki nahi.
ml-logistic-16: Pehle har point pe $\hat p$, phir har point ka loss — ek point ka $y = 0$ hai, doosre ka $y = 1$.
$z = 2x - 1$; loss $= -\ln\hat p$ jab $y = 1$, aur $-\ln(1 - \hat p)$ jab $y = 0$. Average = sum/2.
$x = 0$ pe $z = -1$, $\hat p = \sigma(-1) \approx 0.269$, toh $1 - \hat p \approx 0.731$. Ab doosra point karo. Trap: sum nahi, average chahiye; aur natural log lo.
ml-knn-06: Teen alag $k$ ke liye vote karna hai — distances ek hi baar sort karo, phir top-$k$ gino.
Har point ka distance $|x - 3|$ nikaalo; sort karke pehle 1, 3, 5 points ki classes ka majority lo.
Pehle do: $|3.5 - 3| = 0.5$ aur $|2 - 3| = 1$. Baaki teen distances bhi nikaalo. Trap: 3.5 ka distance 2 se chhota hai — nearest point kaun hai, dhyaan se.
ml-knn-07: Regression hai, classification nahi — 3 nearest points ke $y$ ka mean lena hai.
Squared distance $(x_1 - 1)^2 + (x_2 - 1)^2$ se sort kar sakte ho; order same rehta hai.
P1 aur P2 dono ka squared distance 1 hai. Ab P3, P4, P5 ka nikaalo aur teesra nearest chuno. Trap: saare 5 targets ka average mat lena.
ml-knn-08: Teen points, do metrics — har metric mein nearest point alag ho sakta hai, dono ki list banao.
Query origin hai: Euclidean $\sqrt{x_1^2 + x_2^2}$, Manhattan $|x_1| + |x_2|$.
P ke liye: Euclidean $\sqrt{8}$, Manhattan $4$. Ab Q aur R ke dono distances nikaalo. Trap: diagonal wala point Manhattan mein zyada door lagta hai.
ml-knn-09: Har statement ko chhote example se socho: vote count, distance pe noise, scaling, aur $k = n$.
Prediction sirf neighbours ki **ranking** pe depend karti hai; jo badlaav ranking nahi badalta, wo prediction bhi nahi badalta.
Agar har distance 10 guna ho jaaye, kya sorted order badlega? Aur $k = n$ pe kaunse points chune jaate hain? Trap: uniform scaling aur per-feature scaling alag cheez hain.
ml-knn-10: Scaling pehle, distance baad mein — raw values mein feature 2 hi sab decide karega.
Min–max: $x' = (x - \min)/(\max - \min)$; yahan feature 1 ko 10 se aur feature 2 ko 1000 se divide karna hai.
Scaled $P = (0.2, 0.3)$. Ab $Q$ scale karo aur differences nikaalo. Trap: square root mat bhoolo, aur Manhattan nahi, Euclidean chahiye.
ml-knn-11: $k$ ki value training points ki ginti ke barabar hai — kaun-kaun neighbour banega?
$k = n$ pe har query ke neighbours poora training set hai, toh vote hamesha same rehta hai.
Vote gino: 7 A vs 5 B. Kya ye query ki location se badlega? Trap: nearest point ki class sirf $k = 1$ pe decide karti hai.
ml-knn-12: Har point ko classify karte waqt use training set se hatana hai — warna wo khud ka nearest neighbour ban jaayega.
Har $x$ ke liye baaki paanch mein se nearest point dhoondo aur uski class ko asli class se compare karo.
$x = 1$: nearest 2 (A), sahi. $x = 2$: 1 aur 4 mein se kaun paas hai? Aise hi sab chhe points check karo. Trap: point ko khud se compare mat karna.
ml-knn-13: Do voting rules — ek mein har neighbour ka 1 vote, doosre mein vote $1/d$.
Weighted rule: class $c$ ka score $= \sum 1/d$ over neighbours of class $c$.
Plain vote pehle gino (A ke kitne, B ke kitne). Phir B ka weighted score $1/3 + 1/3$ banao aur A ke $1/1$ se compare karo. Trap: dono rules swap mat karo.
ml-knn-14: Distance yahan Euclidean nahi — kitni positions alag hain, wahi gino.
Har vector ko query 10110 ke saath position-by-position compare karo; 3 sabse chhote counts wale neighbours lo.
T1 = 10010 vs 10110: sirf teesri position alag, distance 1. Ab T2 se T5 tak gino. Trap: chhota Hamming distance = zyada similar; farthest points mat chuno.
ml-knn-15: Table $x$ ke order mein hai, distance ke order mein nahi — pehle $|x - 10|$ se sort karo.
Sorted list pe $k = 1, 3, 5, \dots$ ke liye top-$k$ ka vote gino; jahan pehli baar B jeete wahi chahiye.
Sabse paas: 11 (distance 1, A) aur 8.5 (1.5, A). Aage ke distances nikaal ke list poori karo. Trap: even $k$ pe tie ho sakta hai, aur odd $k$ hi chahiye.
ml-knn-16: Socho k-NN training ke time asal mein kya karta hai — kuch seekhta hai ya bas data rakh leta hai?
Non-parametric = model ka size data ke saath badhta hai; lazy = kaam prediction ke time. 1-NN boundary Voronoi cells se banti hai.
Weight-vector wala option dekho: kaunsa model training mein $w$ seekhta hai — k-NN ya logistic regression? Trap: 1-NN boundary piecewise hai, ek hi line nahi.
